title: Normalization adjunction for a component of a nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], pure of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], not assumed proper or separated. Assume that each nonsmooth closed point has completed local ring $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ (maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], two-variable formal power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]), and that the other points are smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $Z$ be a proper irreducible component of $C$, endowed with its reduced closed subscheme structure, and let $
u: ar Z	o Z$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization]. Then $
u$ is finite and $ ar Z$ is a proper smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves]. If $B_Z$ is the reduced divisor on $ ar Z$ of points lying over the singular points of the ambient curve $C$, then each ambient node has two points on the normalizations of its branches, possibly both on $ ar Z$ when it is a self-node of $Z$; $B_Z$ counts exactly those branches belonging to $Z$. The only singularities of the reduced component $Z$ are its self-nodes; a node where $Z$ meets a different component is smooth as a point of $Z$. The normalization morphism is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of $Z$. For the adjunction line $K_{C/k}$ of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction], restricted along $ ar Z\xrightarrow{
u}Z\hookrightarrow C$, there is a canonical isomorphism $
u^*(K_{C/k}|_Z)\cong\Omega^1_{ ar Z/k}\otimes\mathcal O_{ ar Z}(B_Z)$. Here $\Omega^1_{ ar Z/k}$ is [def-sc-kahler-differentials] and $\mathcal O_{ ar Z}(B_Z)$ is the invertible module of the indicated effective divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-adjunction-preparation] to $C$: it is reduced, its singular set $T$ is finite, and $K_{C/k}$ exists with its smooth-locus identification. A reduced irreducible component $Z$ is integral, finite type and one-dimensional; it is proper by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node) and Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve); assembly of the three re-split inputs.

proof.text: At each $x\in T$, apply [lem-trf-split-node-component-normalization] to $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$: it is reduced by step 1, essentially of finite type, of dimension $1$ as $x$ is a closed point of the pure one-dimensional finite-type $C$, and $\widehat A\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as complete local $k$-algebras by hypothesis. Its two completed normalization branches are the projections to $k[[t]]$. If $x$ has one component both belong to it and its completion is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$; if it has two components each has one branch and completion $k[[t]]$. Localization compatibility assigns these points to the scheme normalizations, giving exactly the asserted counts.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node) and Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve); assembly of the three re-split inputs.

proof.text: Set $S=T\cap Z$, partitioned by these two local types. Outside $S$, a smooth affine neighbourhood in $C$ is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]; after removing the other components it equals $Z$. Apply [lem-trf-completed-curve-boundary-geometry]: $\bar Z$ is smooth proper connected, $\nu$ finite and an isomorphism over $Z_{\rm sm}$, the only singularities are self-nodes, and $B_Z$ is the reduced Cartier inverse image of $S$. Put $L=\nu^*(K_{C/k}|_Z)$ and $M=\Omega^1_{\bar Z/k}\otimes\mathcal O(B_Z)$. Step 1 and the divisor trivialization give $\alpha:L\dashrightarrow M$, an isomorphism off $B_Z$.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node) and Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve); assembly of the three re-split inputs.

proof.text: For $p\in B_Z$, $D=\mathcal O_{\bar Z,p}$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Apply [lem-trf-formal-plane-adjunction-lattice] to the reduced finite-type lci chart of step 1, $f=uv$, and the completed branch of step 2. These are local normalization rings, essentially of finite type with residue $k$. On the $u$ branch $f_v=u$ gives $\mathrm dt/t$; on the $v$ branch $f_u=v$ gives $-\mathrm dt/t$. The lemma compares these through the same generic smooth-locus map and identifies regular completed differentials with $k[[t]]\mathrm dt$. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], $\mathcal O(B_Z)_p=z^{-1}D$ for a uniformizer $z$. Its completed ideal is $(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local]. Thus both completed lattices under $\alpha$ are $k[[t]]\mathrm dt/t$; the sign is a unit, also in characteristic two.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node) and Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve); explicit residue calculation via duality.tex Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), followed by the DVR extension argument.

proof.text: Choose stalk generators and write $\alpha$ as $a=wz^n$ with $w\in D^*$, using [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Equality of the completed lattices forces $n=0$, so $a$ is a unit and extends to a neighbourhood isomorphism. Together with the isomorphism off $B_Z$ these glue: equality at the generic point implies equality of local sections by the same node's injections into $k(\bar Z)$. The extension is unique, hence canonical and independent of formal coordinates. This proves the required isomorphism.
